chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I wrote to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who has a vineyard, can he sell the grapes and the dates to one whom he knows that he will make it into wine or an intoxicant? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He sells it as permissible in the time when its drinking or eating is permissible, so there is no problem with selling it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell grapes to a winemaker in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *asalat al-ibaha* (presumption of permissibility) in commercial transactions, ruling that the sale is valid because the commodity itself is halal at the moment of transfer, regardless of the buyer's subsequent use. This ruling highlights the distinction between the intrinsic nature of the good and the extrinsic action of the consumer, a key concept in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of sales contracts involving potential *khamr*.
